declarations.description:
A box to choose from a list with a search box to filter it by typing: what a `<select>` with many options should be. It is a Web Awesome `wa-select` whose first child is a
search box (a `wa-input`): when it opens the focus goes to the box, typing hides the options that do not match, and the arrows pass from the box to the options that are seen. It is
used where a `<select>` would go: it has `value`, `disabled`, `name` and `required`, takes part in a form, and fires `change` when something is chosen. It chooses only among what it
has: what is typed is for searching, it is not kept. It knows nothing of what the choices are or of any language: everything comes by property. The page loads Web Awesome.

```html
<wax-combobox placeholder="Pick one..." empty-text="Nothing matches"></wax-combobox>
```
```js
combo.choices = [{ value: 'es', label: 'España' }, { value: 'fr', label: 'Francia' }];   // before the value: a value that is not among the choices is dropped
combo.value = 'es';
combo.addEventListener('change', () => use(combo.value));
```

If the choices are not all there and have to be fetched as the user types, listen to `wax-query` and give the new `choices`.

declarations.description:
A card that floats next to what was clicked: in a long list the thing it talks about may be far away, out of sight. With a mouse it can also peek: it shows a moment after the pointer
arrives (`peek`), goes when it leaves (`leave`), and stays once clicked (`show`); clicking the same thing again closes it (`toggle`). Without a mouse there is no "next to": it goes in the
middle with the rest dimmed. Escape, a click outside and its × close it too.

It opens and closes like a `wa-dialog`: the `open` property, `show()` and `hide()`, and four events, `wax-show`, `wax-after-show`, `wax-hide` and `wax-after-hide`. `wax-show` and
`wax-hide` can be cancelled (`preventDefault()` keeps it as it was). It knows nothing of what it shows: the content is its children, which whoever opens it fills in the listener of
`wax-show` (and cancels it if there is nothing to say). It knows nothing of the Back button either: whoever wants Back to close it listens to its events.

```html
<wax-floating-card close-label="Cerrar"></wax-floating-card>   <!-- a child of the body -->
```
```js
card.addEventListener('wax-show', event => {                      // the content, when it is going to show
  card.replaceChildren(dayView(event.detail.anchor.dataset.day));
});
day.addEventListener('click', () => card.toggle(day));            // pinned, next to the day; the same day again closes it
day.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => card.peek(day));         // with a mouse, after a moment
day.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => card.leave());
```

It is placed with the coordinates of the page, so it has to be a child of the `body` (or of an element that is not positioned).

declarations.description:
The usual list to choose from: icon, name and a note per line. One line is selected at a time (click it again to clear), and with Ctrl, Cmd or Shift + click
lines are marked, any number, for the application to do something with them (join them). It knows nothing about what the items are.

```html
<wax-item-list empty="Nothing here"></wax-item-list>
```
```js
list.items = sites.map(s => ({ key: s.id, icon: '🍺', name: s.name, note: `${s.meters} m`, faded: s.hidden }));
list.addEventListener('wax-select', event => open(event.detail.key));   // key is null when the selection is cleared
list.addEventListener('wax-mark', event => join(event.detail.keys));
```

Two things a list can also do, if asked:
- **Move** (`movable`): each line has a handle, dragged with mouse or finger, or moved with the arrow keys when it has the focus; the list gives back the keys in their
  new order (`wax-move`).
- **Swipe** (`swipe-label`): sliding a line sideways with the finger uncovers one action (Remove, Seen) instead of doing it straight away (`wax-swipe`).
